node.statement: Let n be finite, let a,b be real vectors indexed by {1,...,n}, and let S be a family of pairwise disjoint coordinate subsets Q. For d_Q := sum_{j in Q}(a_j-b_j), define S_+ := {Q in S : d_Q >= 0}, S_- := {Q in S : d_Q < 0}, U_+ := union_{Q in S_+}Q, and U_- := union_{Q in S_-}Q. Distinguish the coordinate-set positive mass r^+_coord(U) := sum_{j in U} max(r_j,0) from the fiber-family positive mass r^+_fib(T) := sum_{Q in T} sum_{j in Q} max(r_j,0). Pairwise disjointness gives r^+_coord(U_+) = r^+_fib(S_+) and r^+_coord(U_-) = r^+_fib(S_-), because each coordinate in the respective union occurs in exactly one fiber. Since S_+ and S_- are subfamilies of S and every max(r_j,0) is nonnegative, r^+_fib(S_+) <= r^+_fib(S) and r^+_fib(S_-) <= r^+_fib(S). Hence a^+_coord(U_+) <= a^+_fib(S) and b^+_coord(U_-) <= b^+_fib(S), which are precisely the intended, now type-explicit inequalities in node 1.6.
